The showcase

One program that uses everything the compiler accepts today, beside its output.

This is the voyage of the survey ship Drachma: one program that uses everything the compiler accepts today. Numbers of every width, units of measure carried through math, structs and constructors, enums and match, optionals, failures with handlers and causes, interfaces and generics, borrows and lives, lists, maps, lambdas, and a C library (the harbours of part 6, examples/showcase/c/) called through a safe wrapper. Part 7 is the logbook, which reads and writes JSON with convert and uses the string module. Each part has a header comment saying what it shows off.

It is a real, tested example, and a project of several files: examples/showcase/ has a drachm.toml (with a [native] table for the C helper), src/main.drh and a module for each chapter under src/voyage/, plus src/rules.drh for the constants. main.drh imports them in the different ways a file can (a module, a module under another name, every name under a prefix, names bare as well, single items), and systems.drh reaches rules.drh with a file path that climbs a folder. The expected output is examples/showcase/expect.out. cargo test builds the project on both backends and checks the output, and this page reads all the files when the site is built, so it cannot go out of date. Run it yourself with drachm run examples/showcase.

Select a source tab to switch files. Use Left or Right to move between tabs, or Home and End to jump to the first or last file.

The block below can be resized. Drag the divider between the program and its output (or press its arrow keys), drag the bar under the panes to make the block taller or shorter, and press Expand for a full-screen view (Esc closes it). Each pane scrolls on its own, and long lines scroll sideways.

The dispatch companion runs as a separate script. Run drachm run examples/showcase/dispatch/dispatch.drh to send the survey report to harbour through three relays. Its expected output is in examples/showcase/dispatch/dispatch.out.
